name: MAIA
description: We introduce MAIA (Multimodal AI Assessment), a native-Italian benchmark designed for fine-grained investigation of the reasoning abilities of visual language models on videos. MAIA differs from other available video benchmarks for its design, its reasoning categories, the metric it uses and the language and culture of the videos. It evaluates Vision Language Models (VLMs) on two aligned tasks: a visual statement verification task, and an open-ended visual question-answering task, both on the same set of video-related questions. It considers twelve reasoning categories that aim to disentangle language and vision relations by highlight when one of two alone encodes sufficient information to solve the tasks, when they are both needed and when the full richness of the short video is essential instead of just a part of it. Thanks to its carefully taught design, it evaluates VLMs' consistency and visually grounded natural language comprehension and generation simultaneously through an aggregated metric. Last but not least, the video collection has been carefully selected to reflect the Italian culture and the language data are produced by native-speakers.
evaluation_method: accuracy for verification, exact_match / standard VQA metrics and text-generation metrics (BLEU / F1) for open-ended answers; final results reported as an aggregated composite score
reputation: A recently proposed, language- and culture-specific video-language benchmark (Italian) attracting interest for fine-grained VLM evaluation but not yet widely adopted outside the multimedia-NLP community.
notes: Italian-language and culturally specific video collection; evaluates fine-grained reasoning categories; may be smaller and less diverse than large multilingual video benchmarks; not an LLM-only benchmark (multimodal).
